'''Edward Newman Brandt Jr.''' MD (July 3, 1933 – August 26, 2007) was an American [[physician]], mathematician, and [[public health]] administrator. He was appointed acting [[Surgeon General of the United States|surgeon general of the United States]] from 1981 to 1982 and served as the [[United States Assistant Secretary for Health|United States assistant secretary for health]] from 1981 to 1984.

== Early life and career ==
Born in [[Oklahoma City]], Brandt graduated with an MD and PhD in biostatistics from the [[University of Oklahoma]] School of Medicine.<ref name="umaryland">{{cite web |url=http://um.umaryland.edu/about/past-presidents-of-the-university-of-maryland-baltimore/edward-n-brandt-jr-md-phd/ |title=Past Presidents of the University of Maryland, Baltimore: Edward N. Brandt Jr., MD, PhD |work=University of Maryland |year=2014 |access-date=July 29, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130407003534/http://um.umaryland.edu/about/past-presidents-of-the-university-of-maryland-baltimore/edward-n-brandt-jr-md-phd/ |archive-date=April 7, 2013 }}</ref> He was a faculty member from his alma mater from 1961 to 1970 before moving to the [[University of Texas]] at [[Galveston, Texas|Galveston]] (1970–1981), [[University of Maryland]] at [[Baltimore]] (1981–1989), and [[University of Oklahoma]] School of Medicine (1989–2007).<ref name="umaryland"/>

== Death ==
Brandt died of lung cancer on August 26, 2007; he was 74 years old.<ref name="boston">{{cite news |url=http://archive.boston.com/news/globe/obituaries/articles/2007/09/09/edward_brandt_jr_74_led_fight_in_early_days_of_aids/ |title=Edward Brandt Jr., 74; led fight in early days of AIDS |first=Thomas H.  |last=Maugh II |work=[[The Boston Globe]] |date=September 9, 2007 |publisher=[[New York Times Company|NYTC]] |location=[[Boston, MA|Boston]] |issn=0743-1791 |access-date=July 29, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2007-sep-05-me-brandt5-story.html | work=Los Angeles Times | first=Thomas H. | last=Maugh II | date=September 5, 2007 | title=Dr. Edward Brandt Jr., 74; official oversaw first federal response to AIDS}}</ref> His papers were donated to the [[National Library of Medicine]]. <ref>{{cite web|url=https://findingaids.nlm.nih.gov/repositories/ammp/resources/brandt573|title=Edward Brandt Assistant Secretary for Health Speech Collection 1981–1984|publisher=National Library of Medicine}}</ref>
